sections.name: ShareController (part 1)
sections.title: Create, list and revoke routes
sections.what: Creates a share link, limited to 10 requests a minute. Lists the user's share links. Revokes one by id with a patch route, and a delete route that does the same revoke.
sections.why: Likely reason: the delete route may exist for clients that expect a delete action. The code does not say.
sections.watch_out: The delete route does not delete anything. It sets the revoked flag, so the record stays.

sections.name: ShareController (part 2)
sections.title: Public view route
sections.what: Open route that shows the shared records for a token, limited to 20 requests a minute. The audit description says each view is recorded.
sections.why: Likely reason: doctors need to view records without an account.
sections.watch_out: Anyone holding the full token can read the patient's records until it expires or is revoked, and the token is visible in the address.

summary: Exposes the web routes for creating, listing and revoking doctor share links, plus the public route a doctor uses to view shared records.
purpose: Lets a patient manage share links, and lets a doctor open a link without having an account.
why: Likely reason: the public route exists because doctors do not sign in. Other reasons are not stated in the code.
how: Routes for the signed-in user pass their id to the share service. The public route takes the token from the address and returns the shared bundle. Create and view routes have rate limits.
inputs: Signed-in user id, share id, the request body for creating a share, the token in the address, and request details used for the audit record.
outputs: JSON replies with success and data, a list of shares, or a revoke result.
risks: The token is in the web address, so it can be written to server or proxy logs. The delete route only revokes and does not remove the record, despite the name. The public route needs no sign-in, so the token is the only check.
debug: For a 404 on the public route, check the token is correct and the share exists. For a 403, check whether it was revoked or expired. For 429 errors, the rate limit was reached. For revoke problems, check the share id belongs to the signed-in user.
